title: Bar model template
subject: Mathematics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 43 (Bar model template (printable, in the pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 43: Fraction problems in context. To understand how to choose the right fraction calculation in a word problem

questions.q: A recipe uses 3/4 kg of flour and 1/3 kg of sugar. What is the total mass?
A ribbon is 5 m. 2 3/4 m is cut off. How much is left?
3/8 of a box of 64 dates are eaten. How many are left?
In a madrasah 2/5 of pupils are in Year 7 and 1/4 in Year 8. What fraction are in other years?
(a) Add 1 1/2 litres and 2 2/3 litres (b) 5/9 of 81 kg (c) Saad reads 1/3 of a book on Monday and 2/5 on Tuesday. What fraction is left?
Of £240, a family gives 1/8 in sadaqah and spends 2/3 of the rest on food. How much is left?
After spending 3/5 of his money, Omar has £14 left. How much did he start with?
A bag holds 40 sweets; 3/8 are red. How many are not red?
1/2 + 1/5 of a field is planted. What fraction is not planted?
Big question: how did the bar model help in one problem today?
questions.a: For example it showed the 'rest' as the remaining parts of the bar, so I knew what to find a fraction of.
